I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. I'm 71 now — my back isn't good, my son is working in Shijiazhuang, so I manage mostly alone with some hired machinery help from the village service station.

**My reasoning:**

I grow winter wheat and summer maize. That's what I know. That's what everyone here grows. The two fit together perfectly — wheat goes in October, comes out in June, then I plant corn right after on the same land. No land wasted. No experiments. I've tried other things before and it never ended well.

I have about 5 mu of contracted land. That's manageable for me at my age. I hire the village machinery cooperative to do the rotary tilling before wheat seeding and to harvest both crops. I can't do that work by hand anymore.

For wheat seed, I use the improved variety — Jimai 22 or whatever the township agronomist distributed last year. Not traditional, not the most expensive hybrid. The middle option. For corn, I always buy hybrid seed bags from the agricultural supply shop in town — everyone does, the yield difference is obvious.

Fertilizer: I apply a compound base fertilizer before wheat planting, then urea in March when the wheat starts jointing. For corn I broadcast urea before the big rain in July. I probably use more nitrogen than I should — my father did it this way, I do it this way.

Irrigation: I share a well with two neighbors. Wheat needs water three times — before winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading. Corn usually gets by on summer rain, maybe one pump if August is dry.

Pesticides: I spray wheat twice — herbicide in winter and something for the rust and aphids in spring. Corn once, for the fall armyworm they've been warning about lately.
